video_caption: The video presents a split screen showing two distinct scenes. On the left, in a formal indoor setting with a blue curtain backdrop and four American flags, former President Donald Trump, wearing a dark suit and red tie, walks towards and then stands behind a wooden podium bearing the Presidential Seal. He places a piece of paper on the podium and begins to speak, occasionally gesturing with his left hand. Behind him, several individuals stand attentively, including a man in a dark suit and red tie with his hands clasped, and others in suits and military-style attire, one notably wearing a red beret. On the right side of the screen, a male news anchor, dressed in a dark blue suit and light blue tie, speaks directly to the camera, gesturing with his hands against a blurred backdrop of a cityscape at dusk. A white and gray banner at the bottom of the screen repeatedly displays "THE BEAT WITH ARI MELBER" in blue and gray text.

The video segment opens with a split screen: on the left, Donald Trump, dressed in a dark suit with a white shirt and red tie, speaks at a podium with a serious expression, flanked by four American flags and two other individuals, one in military attire. The presidential seal is visible on the podium. This scene transitions to a "SATURDAY NIGHT LIVE" (NBC) clip showing two men at a news desk; the one on the left, with short grey hair and a dark suit and red tie, smiles and makes a peace sign gesture, then shakes hands with the man on the right, who has dark hair and wears a dark suit and tie. Both men are smiling against a background of a world map. This comedic scene then briefly switches to a pixelated or mosaic-like abstract black and white image on the left, before finally displaying Pablo Picasso's "GUERNICA" painting, identified by text on the top left. Throughout all these transitions on the left side, the right side of the screen consistently features news anchor Ari Melber, with dark hair, wearing a blue suit and light blue tie, speaking directly to the camera and gesturing with his hands, against a blurred nighttime city skyline. The show's title, "THE BEAT WITH ARI MELBER," is displayed repeatedly in the lower third of the screen.

The video begins with a scene from the film "Mystic River," showing a young girl in a white communion dress and veil with her hands clasped in what appears to be a church, surrounded by other children and adults; text on screen reads "MYSTIC RIVER WARNER BROS.". The scene then cuts to a distressed woman in a white robe running down a wooden staircase, followed by a man in a dark jacket standing in a dimly lit doorway. Next, a book cover titled "BOB HONEY WHO JUST DO STUFF" by "SEAN PENN" is displayed against a white background with blue geometric patterns. The cover features a black and white image of a man's face with colorful, hand-drawn elements like a house, a nuclear explosion, and a hammer. The video then transitions to a news anchor, a man in a blue suit and tie, speaking directly to the camera with a city skyline background and "THE BEAT WITH ARI MELBER" graphics. Finally, the scene shows Sean Penn, a man with a mustache and a blue denim shirt, smiling subtly and looking off-camera, sitting in a studio setting with "BEAT" visible on a screen in the background.

The video opens with a two-shot of Sean Penn (left, wearing a light blue denim shirt and brown pants, with tousled brown hair and a mustache) and interviewer Ari Melber (right, in a dark suit and blue tie) seated at a clear glass-top table in a newsroom setting. Penn gestures with his hands as he speaks, while Melber listens attentively, occasionally nodding. Two white mugs with "BEAT" written on them are on the table, along with a stack of papers. The background features a large screen with a cityscape and the word "BEAT," as well as a view of a bustling newsroom with various screens and desks. The glass table has a red base. The scene then transitions to a split screen: Ari Melber remains on the right, looking at a video clip of Donald Trump (on the left, wearing a dark suit and striped tie, speaking from behind a table with flags in the background). Text overlays on the bottom read: "THE BEAT WITH ARI MELBER". This split-screen segment briefly changes to show Trump at a different moment, signing a document with several people standing behind him. The video then cuts to a close-up of Sean Penn speaking, maintaining a serious expression, with the newsroom as his background.

The video segment opens with a shot of two men seated at a clear glass desk in a modern television studio. On the left, Sean Penn, dressed in a light blue denim shirt and dark pants, sits attentively with his hands clasped, listening to the interviewer. On the right, the interviewer, Ari Melber, wearing a dark suit and tie, holds a piece of paper and looks toward Penn while speaking. Two white mugs with "BEAT" written in blue are on the desk, along with a newspaper. A clear plastic partition stands between the two men. Behind Melber, a large screen displays a city skyline and a bridge at night, with "THE BEAT" logo prominently featured. The background behind Penn shows an office space with red lighting accents. The scene then transitions to a graphic displaying the cover of Sean Penn's book, "BOB HONEY WHO JUST DO STUFF," which features a stylized, somewhat obscured face with chaotic, colorful imagery, alongside a blue text box containing a quote in white: "Many wonderful American people in pain and rage elected you. Many Russians did, too... Though the office will remain real, you never were nor will be." The graphic has a light blue and white background with abstract square patterns and the text "THE BEAT WITH ARI MELBER" at the bottom. The video then cuts back to the live interview, with Penn still listening intently, occasionally nodding, while Melber gestures slightly with his left hand as he speaks.

The video opens with a close-up of Sean Penn, a middle-aged man with a mustache and slightly disheveled brown hair, wearing a light blue denim button-up shirt, speaking directly to the camera with a serious expression in a studio setting where "NBC NEWS" and "BEAT" logos are visible in the background. The scene then transitions to a split screen: on the right, Penn (back to the camera, wearing the same shirt) is seen sitting across a table from a man in a dark suit and blue tie (Ari Melber), with "THE BEAT WITH ARI MELBER" text and a city skyline graphic in the background, while on the left, a montage of clips from the movie "Milk" plays, featuring Sean Penn portraying Harvey Milk in various situations—smiling, interacting with crowds, shaking hands, swimming, and speaking passionately into a megaphone during protests, with signs visible including "OUR HUMAN RIGHTS" and "WE ARE YOUR." During these "Milk" clips, a yellow box in the top-left corner displays the text "'MILK' FOCUS FEATURES," and a blurred image of Donald Trump appears momentarily in the background of a protest scene. Throughout the split-screen, Penn on the right continues to speak, maintaining a contemplative demeanor.

The video segment opens with a split screen, showing former President Donald Trump on the left, first raising his right fist, then clapping, while standing in front of an American flag and a blue backdrop with "TRUMP PENCE" in white text. On the right, a man in a dark suit (Ari Melber) is speaking. The scene then transitions to a studio setting where actor Sean Penn, with wavy brown hair and a mustache, wearing a light blue denim shirt, sits opposite Ari Melber at a transparent table, engaging in a conversation. "BEAT" logos and city lights are visible in the background. As Penn speaks, the screen splits again, with clips from the movie "The Dark Knight" appearing on the left, showcasing scenes with Batman's vehicle and the Joker, accompanied by the text "'THE DARK KNIGHT' WARNER BROS" at the top left, while Sean Penn continues to speak and gesture on the right side of the screen.

The video opens with a close-up of an older man, Sean Penn, who has dark, slightly dishevelled hair and a mustache, wearing a light blue denim button-up shirt. He looks serious and pensive, gazing to the right side of the frame. The background is a blurred modern studio setting with "NBC" and repeated, partially visible "BEAT" text. The scene then cuts to a wider shot, showing Sean Penn from behind, still in the light blue denim shirt, seated at a desk. Across from him sits a younger man in a dark blue suit, light blue tie, and white pocket square, looking down at papers on the desk. Two white mugs with blue logos are on the table, one clearly showing "THE BEAT WITH ARI MELBER". Behind them, a stylized city skyline at night is displayed on a large screen, along with the prominent words "THE BEAT" and the "NBC" logo.

In a modern newsroom setting with glass partitions and rows of computers in the background, two men sit opposite each other at a clear glass desk. The man on the left, wearing a blue denim shirt, listens intently with a smile on his face. The man on the right, dressed in a dark suit, gestures with his hands before picking up a large newspaper advertisement and holding it up, revealing its content to the camera. The ad prominently displays the title "BOB HONEY WHO JUST DO STUFF" by "SEAN PENN" and boasts "INSTANT NATIONAL BESTSELLER!" with the headline "THE CRITICS AGREE!" It features a series of humorously negative quotes about the book, such as "Honestly, shut your face, Sean Penn." (from Marie Claire), "Sean Penn the novelist must be stopped." (The New York Times), "Ignore Penn." (The Guardian), "Is Bob Honey wildly offensive? Reader, it is." (Publishers Weekly), "Entertaining and maddening in equal measure." (The Washington Post), "Perplexing and unquantifiable by design." (The New Yorker), "Repellent on one level, but stupid on so many others." (The Guardian), and "Very manly." (Esquire), followed by the invitation "READ IT AND DECIDE FOR YOURSELF." Below these, smaller text mentions other readers including Salmane Rushdie and Sarah Silverman. The man in the suit laughs as he holds the ad, and the man in the denim shirt smiles and nods in response. On the table are several white mugs with blue rims, each featuring a "BEAT" logo. The camera then zooms in on the smiling face of the man in the denim shirt.

The video opens with a split screen, displaying a film clip on the left and a man speaking on the right. The film clip, labeled at the top left with "CARLITO'S WAY" and "UNIVERSAL PICTURES," shows a man in a light suit walking through a fenced parking lot. The man on the right has shoulder-length brown hair, a denim shirt, and is speaking directly to the camera with a slight smile and occasional hand gestures. The film clip then transitions to a close-up of a man with curly red hair and glasses wearing a light suit, looking contemplative, followed by a wider shot of him interacting with another man in a green shirt across a table. Throughout these film clips, the man in the denim shirt on the right continues to speak. The scene then shifts to a full-screen shot of the man in the denim shirt, now with a more serious but amused expression, sitting in what appears to be a news studio. He concludes his thought, then the camera widens to show him sitting at a glass desk opposite a man in a dark suit, presumably an interviewer. Both men are smiling and laughing as they look at each other, with the words "THE BEAT WITH ARI MELBER" visible in blue and white lettering on the desk and in the background.

The video features an interview between two men at a clear glass table in a newsroom. The man on the left, Sean Penn, wears a light blue denim shirt and an earphone, listening intently and occasionally sipping from a white mug with a blue "BEAT" logo. The man on the right, the interviewer in a dark blue suit and patterned blue tie, actively speaks and gestures, holding papers and a small book on the table beside two "BEAT" mugs. The background reveals a modern newsroom with numerous computer monitors and glass partitions. The scene transitions to clips from a "60 MINUTES" (CBS - JAN. 2016) report, showing tactical teams in military gear conducting a raid, followed by footage of El Chapo being led away by military personnel, one of whom has "EJERCITO MEXICANO" (Mexican Army) written on his uniform. This is followed by a close-up of Sean Penn speaking during what appears to be the "60 Minutes" interview. The video then returns to the newsroom interview, with the interviewer presenting a news graphic that displays El Chapo and a "DAILY NEWS" headline stating: "Prosecutors in El Chapo's trial seek to block jurors from seeing Sean Penn's sympathetic Rolling Stone interview," with an additional text box reading: "JURORS WOULD "DRAW SYMPATHY" FOR THE DEFENDANT EL CHAPO." The interviewer then focuses on this development, asking Penn questions while looking at him and gesturing.

The video features actor Sean Penn, with a mustache and wearing a denim shirt, speaking to the camera. The initial frames present a split screen, with Penn on the right and various B-roll clips on the left, all bearing the text "EL UNIVERSAL" (English: The Universal). These clips show a dilapidated rural building with a dirt path, a small propeller plane flying in a blue sky, people gathered around a blue car (including a woman in dark sunglasses and clothing, and a man in a light shirt), the same woman in sunglasses interacting with a staff member inside what appears to be an airport terminal near a "no smoking" sign, and finally, Sean Penn himself, wearing a dark jacket and cap, walking through an indoor space. Penn is then shown in a closer shot, alone, speaking directly to the camera with a serious expression. The video concludes with Penn, still in his denim shirt, seated at a clear glass table across from a male interviewer in a suit, in a studio setting with a cityscape and "THE BEAT WITH ARI MELBER" (English: The Beat with Ari Melber) branding visible in the background.

The video begins with a man in a navy suit and light blue tie, presumably Ari Melber, holding a book titled "BOB HONEY WHO JUST DO STUFF" (BOB HONEY WHO JUST DO STUFF) and smiling while speaking directly to the camera. The background is a blue graphic of a city skyline with "THE BEAT WITH ARI MELBER" written on it. The scene then cuts to a different man, Sean Penn, wearing a denim shirt, smiling and then shaking hands with the first man. He has a slight mustache and appears to be laughing. The background behind him shows glimpses of "BEAT L BEAT" graphics. Following a brief black screen, the video transitions to an end card featuring a man in a dark suit, tie, and glasses speaking, with a city night skyline visible through a window behind him. On the right side of the screen, the text "WATCH MORE" is displayed, and below the speaker, "SUBSCRIBE" is visible. The man gestures with his right hand, pointing towards the right side of the screen.
